headline: Going Commando gains matching code across boot, levels and regional versions
summary: Contributors landed matching C for boot and level routines, including the lock-on tether family and work in Yeedil and Aranos Prison (#384, #386, #387). Matching means the C compiles to the original game's bytes; the final snapshot records 7,760 of 8,579 functions and 4,684,272 of 5,527,936 code bytes, about 84.74% of code by size, for USA v1.01. Functional C intended for the native port remains in unmerged draft #389 and adds no matches to these figures.
highlights: #386 reports USA v2.00 at 7,586 of 8,634 functions and 80.93% matched code, and Europe/Australia at 6,992 of 8,672 functions and 54.14% matched code at its stated measurement commit.
The 453-function batch covers boot and level code; another batch adds matching routines in Yeedil and Aranos Prison and repairs regional compatibility (#384, #387).
A shared helper matches at every USA v1.01 placement; five measured near misses remain, and USA v2.00 needs generated fallbacks for it and callers (#388).
